comments.note: settings.js has grown to 4 sections with consistent but inline patterns. If a 5th+ section is added, consider a shared buildNumberInputRow(labelText, inputOpts, unitText) helper to eliminate the label/input/unit triple construction repeated in both buildRefreshDelaySection and the new buildNotesDisplaySection.

The credentials section in renderSettings() is built inline (not via a builder function) unlike the other three sections which return {element, save}. This inconsistency makes the renderSettings() body harder to scan. Future work could extract buildCredentialsSection() following the same pattern.

The showLoading() function in settings.js uses innerHTML for its loading indicator template (line 124), which is an exception to the textContent-only XSS safety rule. The strings are static literals with no user data, so there is no actual XSS risk, but it is inconsistent with the otherwise strict textContent convention used throughout the file.

comments.note: save() in buildNotesDisplaySection() accepts any integer in-range (e.g. 125 px), not just multiples of 10, because the JS validation only checks Number.isInteger() + range bounds. The HTML step=10 attribute enforces multiples in the browser UI, and server-side validation should handle non-multiples. This is consistent with how buildRefreshDelaySection() handles its step attribute. No action required.
No unit label rendered beside the Columns input (by design — the AC does not require one). This matches the WP spec. Noted here for reviewers scanning the rendered output.
